headline: OpenLogi brings local control to Logitech mice with 44 actions and zero telemetry.
summary: OpenLogi is a native, local-first macOS alternative to Logitech Options+, written in Rust. It enables binding 44 built-in actions, custom shortcuts, and app launchers to mouse buttons without cloud accounts or telemetry.
details: OpenLogi is a new macOS application designed as a native, local-first alternative to Logitech Options+. Written in Rust, it allows users to customize their Logitech mouse buttons with 44 built-in actions, custom shortcuts, and app launchers, all without any telemetry or cloud account requirements.

The software offers extensive customization, letting users bind specific actions to each physical button on their Logitech device. This per-device configuration ensures tailored control, whether for productivity tasks or complex scripted actions.

Operating over HID++ via Bolt, Bluetooth, or wired connections, OpenLogi provides a robust and private way to manage mouse functionality. It is open-source, released under MIT and Apache-2.0 licenses, emphasizing transparency and community contribution.

headline: Block open-sources Berd, a desktop AI agent workspace for macOS, Windows, Linux
summary: Berd provides a single, locally installed environment for working with AI agents across various models and tools, complete with persistent conversation history.
details: Block, the company behind Square and Cash App, has open-sourced Berd, a new desktop application. Berd provides a unified workspace for interacting with various AI agents and models. It's available now on GitHub under an Apache 2.0 license for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

Berd is designed as a desktop-first application, allowing direct interaction with local files, projects, and tools. It emphasizes visible operational state, ensuring users always know which project, agent, model, and session are active, distinguishing it from generic chatbots.

The application originated from Block's internal need to streamline workflows for its employees, who were using different capable agents like Goose, Anthropic's Claude Code, and OpenAI's Codex. Berd offers a consistent environment across these diverse AI tools.

Users can initiate chats, attach files or folders, select agents and models, and work within persistent projects. Berd also allows configuration of AI providers, management of skills and extensions, review of session history, and building automations.

Berd takes a unique approach to agent identity by assigning roles, instructions, skills, and distinct visual identities (like "Gloopies" avatars) to agents. Predefined personas such as Berdy, Pushback, and Choosey are built around different work styles.

This visual layer helps users recognize and differentiate specialized agents at a glance, serving as a functional shorthand for their specific instructions and tools. This becomes increasingly important when juggling multiple agents simultaneously.
